mcqs.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies subject‑verb agreement?

options.A: The committee have decided to postpone the meeting.
options.B: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting.
options.C: The committee were deciding to postpone the meeting.
options.D: The committee deciding to postpone the meeting.

mcqs.answer: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting.
mcqs.explanation: ‘Committee’ is a collective noun treated as singular in formal English, so the singular verb ‘has’ is required. Option A uses the plural verb ‘have’, which is incorrect. Options C and D are grammatically incomplete.

mcqs.question: Fill in the blank with the correct article: "_____ Eiffel Tower is one of the most visited monuments in Paris."
mcqs.explanation: ‘Eiffel Tower’ is a specific, unique landmark, so the definite article ‘the’ is required. ‘A’ and ‘an’ are indefinite articles and cannot be used with a unique proper noun. No article would be incorrect in this context.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct preposition: "She is interested ___ learning new languages."
mcqs.explanation: The verb ‘interested’ collocates with the preposition ‘in’ to indicate the object of interest. ‘At’, ‘on’, and ‘for’ do not form the correct idiomatic expression.

mcqs.question: Select the conjunction that best connects the two clauses: "He wanted to go for a walk, ___ it started to rain."
mcqs.explanation: ‘But’ introduces a contrast between his desire to walk and the rain that prevented it. ‘And’ would add, not contrast; ‘so’ would indicate cause‑effect; ‘or’ would suggest an alternative.

mcqs.question: Which sentence contains a dependent (subordinate) clause?

options.A: I will call you when I arrive.
options.C: The sun rises in the east.

mcqs.answer: I will call you when I arrive.
mcqs.explanation: The phrase ‘when I arrive’ cannot stand alone and depends on the main clause ‘I will call you’; therefore it is a dependent clause. The other sentences consist only of independent clauses.

mcqs.question: Identify the sentence that is written in the passive voice.

options.B: The meal was cooked by the chef.
options.C: The chef is cooking the meal.

mcqs.answer: The meal was cooked by the chef.
mcqs.explanation: In the passive voice, the object of the action becomes the subject and the verb phrase includes a form of ‘be’ plus a past participle (‘was cooked’). Option B meets this pattern. Options A and C are active; D is nonsensical.

mcqs.question: Convert the direct speech into correct indirect speech: "She said, 'I will finish the report tomorrow.'"

options.A: She said that she will finish the report tomorrow.
options.B: She said that she would finish the report the next day.
options.C: She said that I will finish the report tomorrow.
options.D: She said that she finishes the report tomorrow.

mcqs.answer: She said that she would finish the report the next day.
mcqs.explanation: When reporting speech, the verb tense shifts back (will → would) and the time reference changes (tomorrow → the next day). Option B follows these rules. Option A retains the original tense; C changes the subject; D uses present simple incorrectly.

mcqs.question: Read the sentence: "Each of the students have completed their assignments." Which grammatical error does it contain?
mcqs.explanation: The subject ‘Each of the students’ is singular, so the verb should be singular ‘has’, not plural ‘have’. The other options do not describe any problem in this sentence.
